title: Break up the Department of Homeland Security
proposal: The chapter's main recommendation is that the President seek legislation to dismantle DHS, splitting it along mission lines and closing remaining support offices.
quote: Breaking up the department along its mission lines would facilitate mission focus and provide opportunities to reduce overhead

title: Create one Cabinet-level border and immigration agency
proposal: CBP, ICE, USCIS, HHS's Office of Refugee Resettlement, and DOJ's immigration courts and Office of Immigration Litigation should be combined into a single Cabinet-level agency; as fallbacks, merge ICE, CBP and USCIS, or just ICE and CBP.
quote: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) be combined with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE); U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)

title: Move CISA to the Department of Transportation
proposal: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency should be moved out of DHS to the Department of Transportation.
quote: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) be moved to the Department of Transportation.

title: Move FEMA to Interior or Transportation
proposal: FEMA should be moved to the Department of the Interior, or to the Department of Transportation if combined with CISA.
quote: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) be moved to the Department of the Interior or, if combined with CISA, to the Department of Transportation.

title: Move the Coast Guard to DOJ or DOD
proposal: The Coast Guard should move to the Justice Department, and to Defense during a full-scale war; or alternatively to Defense for all purposes.
quote: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) be moved to DOJ and, in time of full-scale war (i.e., threatening the homeland), to the Department of Defense (DOD).

title: Split the Secret Service between DOJ and Treasury
proposal: The Secret Service should be divided, with protection moving to DOJ and financial crime enforcement moving to Treasury.
quote: The U.S. Secret Service (USSS) be divided in two, with the protective element moved to DOJ and the financial enforcement element moved to the Department of the Treasury.

title: Move DHS science office to DOD and WMD office to FBI
proposal: DHS's Science and Technology Directorate should move to the Defense Department, and its Office of Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction should move to the FBI.
quote: The Science and Technology Directorate (S&T) be moved to DOD and the Office of Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction be moved to the FBI.

title: Privatize TSA airport screening
proposal: TSA screening should be privatized, either by expanding the Screening Partnership Program to all airports or by a Canadian-style government corporation hiring private contractors, with TSA setting rules.
quote: These opportunities include privatizing TSA screening and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) National Flood Insurance Program

title: Return CISA to a narrow mission
proposal: CISA should go back to its narrow legal mission of protecting federal networks and coordinating critical infrastructure security.
quote: A conservative Administration should return CISA to its statutory and important but narrow mission.

title: Shift most disaster costs from FEMA to states
proposal: FEMA emergency spending should be reformed so states and localities pay most disaster preparedness and response costs, leaving FEMA to focus on large disasters.
quote: reforming FEMA emergency spending to shift the majority of preparedness and response costs to states and localities

title: End most DHS grant programs
proposal: Most DHS grant programs, which FEMA manages, should be eliminated; the chapter says this requires Congress to act.
quote: localities instead of the federal government, eliminating most of DHS’s grant

title: Remove all unions at DHS, including TSA
proposal: All unions in DHS should be removed for national security reasons, with TSA's workforce de-unionized immediately until it is privatized.
quote: and removing all unions in the department for national security purposes.

title: Give the DHS Secretary a dedicated political team
proposal: The DHS Secretary should have a dedicated team of political appointees chosen by the Office of Presidential Personnel, not detailees.
quote: A key first step for the Secretary to improve front-office functions is to have his or her own dedicated team of political

title: Install nominees as 'acting' leaders during confirmation
proposal: The administration should place nominees for key DHS jobs into similar positions as 'acting' officials while they await Senate confirmation.
quote: the next Administration arguably should place its nominees for key positions into similar positions as “actings”

title: End Senate confirmation for lower-level DHS posts
proposal: Legislation should remove the Senate confirmation requirement for lower-level DHS positions.
quote: The department should also look to remove lower-level but nevertheless important positions that currently require Senate confirmation from the confirmation requirement

title: Political-only line of succession at DHS
proposal: Legislation should set a line of succession in which positions held by career employees count as vacant so a political appointee becomes acting leader, with acting Secretaries able to finalize rules.
quote: where a career employee holds a leadership position in the department, that position should be deemed vacant for line-of-succession purposes

title: 'Soft close' unneeded DHS offices
proposal: The Secretary should use existing authority to 'soft close' ineffective offices by shifting their staff and money to core missions.
quote: The Secretary therefore can and should use his or her inherent, discretionary leadership authority to “soft close” ineffective and problematic corners of the department.

title: Move DHS law enforcement staff from offices to the field
proposal: All DHS staff with law enforcement authority should be moved immediately from office jobs to field jobs.
quote: All personnel with law enforcement capacity should be removed immediately from office billets and deployed to field billets

title: Condition FEMA grants on immigration law compliance
proposal: To get FEMA grants (except disaster aid), applicants should certify they follow federal immigration law, honor ICE detainers, and use E-Verify, and states must share law enforcement information.
quote: Certification by applicants that they comply with all aspects of federal immigration laws, including the honoring of all immigration detainers.

title: Require states to share DMV and voter data for grants
proposal: States and localities seeking DHS grants should commit to full information-sharing, including access to motor vehicle and voter registration databases.
quote: This would include access to department of motor vehicles and voter registration databases.

title: Do not raise H-2B seasonal worker visas above the cap
proposal: The DHS Secretary should not use discretionary authority to raise the number of H-2B seasonal non-farm worker visas above the cap set by law.
quote: The Secretary should make it clear that he or she will not use the Secretary’s existing discretionary authority to increase the number of H-2B

title: Stop regulations supporting the 'H-2 eligible' country list
proposal: The Secretary should not issue rules supporting the list of countries whose citizens are eligible for H-2 guest worker visas.
quote: The Secretary should not issue any regulations in support of the “H-2 eligible” country list

title: Answer unfulfilled congressional and public records requests
proposal: The Secretary should assume past congressional inquiries and public information requests went unanswered and work to fulfill them.
quote: The Secretary should proceed from the assumption that congressional inquiries and public information requests were unfulfilled and then seek to fulfill them.

title: Replace the whole Homeland Security Advisory Committee
proposal: The Secretary should quickly remove and replace all current members of the Homeland Security Advisory Committee.
quote: The Secretary should plan to quickly remove all current members of the Homeland Security Advisory Committee

title: Require CBP to publish border data regularly
proposal: DHS should lift limits on CBP publishing border data and issue a rule requiring CBP to regularly publish accurate border security data without leadership review.
quote: DHS should issue a regulation mandating that CBP publish accurate and timely border security data, readily available to the public

title: Let CBP and DHS leaders use agency aircraft
proposal: The White House should allow CBP and DHS executives to use the agency's own aircraft for official travel.
quote: The White House should grant the authority for CBP and DHS executives to utilize component aviation assets under the Office of Air and Marine (OAM).

title: Merge Border Patrol and Air and Marine Operations
proposal: Border Patrol and CBP's Office of Air and Marine should be combined within CBP.
quote: Border Patrol (BP) and OAM should be combined within CBP . BP has more than

title: Restart horseback Border Patrol and clear accused agents
proposal: CBP should restart and expand horseback Border Patrol units, and the Secretary should clear the records of agents accused of whipping migrants and issue an apology.
quote: CBP should restart and expand use of the horseback-mounted Border Patrol.

title: Merge CBP's Office of Trade into Field Operations
proposal: The Secretary should combine CBP's Office of Trade and Trade Relations with its Office of Field Operations.
quote: The Secretary should combine the Office of Trade (OT) and Trade Relations with the Office of Field Operations (OFO).

title: Limit CBP Notices to Appear and end Notices to Report
proposal: CBP should usually hand migrants to ICE rather than issue Notices to Appear, except in humanitarian cases, and should stop using Notices to Report entirely.
quote: CBP should issue NTAs only in limited situations for humanitarian reasons, such as medical emergencies. In addition, CBP should eliminate use of Notices to Report (NTR) altogether.

title: One national detention standard that allows tents
proposal: A single nationwide detention standard should be written into law so states cannot impose their own, and it should allow wide use of temporary facilities such as tents.
quote: A single nationwide detention standard should be codified that prevents individual states from mandating that federal government agencies adhere

title: Fully budget for migrant processing costs at CBP
proposal: The President should request a CBP budget that fully covers temporary facilities and care, transport, and processing of migrants.
quote: The next President should request a realistic budget that fully pays for these costs.

title: Fund support staff so Border Patrol agents return to the field
proposal: Border Patrol should get more money to hire support staff so agents are freed from processing paperwork.
quote: Increased funding is needed for BP to hire additional support personnel, which would relieve uniformed BP agents from administrative duties

title: Fund upgrades at land ports of entry
proposal: Congress should fund upgrades and new inspection technology, staff, and facilities at key land ports of entry.
quote: Congress should increase funding for facility upgrades at strategic land Ports of Entry (POEs)

title: Stop closing pending immigration cases
proposal: ICE should stop closing out or administratively closing pending immigration court cases and apply immigration law as written.
quote: Order ICE to stop closing out pending immigration cases and apply the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) as written by Congress.

title: Take custody of criminal noncitizens flagged through 287(g)
proposal: ICE should take custody of all noncitizens identified by 287(g) partner police who have records for felonies, violent crimes, DUIs, prior removals, or other serious crimes.
quote: ICE should be directed to take custody of all aliens with records for felonies, crimes of violence, DUIs, previous removals

title: Eliminate T and U visas for crime and trafficking victims
proposal: T and U visas for trafficking and crime victims should be eliminated, with the S visa used for cooperating witnesses; until then, eligibility should be sharply restricted.
quote: Eliminate T and U visas. Victimization should not be a basis for an immigration benefit.

title: Tighten immigration bond rules and reform Alternatives to Detention
proposal: ICE should issue clear guidance on detention and bond and significantly reform the Alternatives to Detention program.
quote: poorly worded bond regulations, contradictory bond policy memoranda, and poor practices for managing released aliens and the Alternatives to Detention (ATD) Program, which requires significant reform.

title: Cut student visas for students from 'enemy nations'
proposal: ICE should put national security first in the student visa program and work with State to eliminate or greatly reduce visas for students from enemy nations.
quote: working with the Department of State to eliminate or significantly reduce the number of visas issued to foreign students from enemy nations.

title: Refocus HSI on immigration-related crime
proposal: Homeland Security Investigations agents should focus mainly on immigration and border crimes such as smuggling and trafficking, handing other cases to other agencies.
quote: Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Special Agents in the 1811 series should enforce Title 8 and 18 crimes as the biggest part of their portfolio.

title: Expand ICE civil arrests nationwide
proposal: ICE removal officers should be made primarily responsible for civil immigration arrests, detention, and removal anywhere in the U.S., without a warrant where appropriate, and ICE should drop self-imposed limits on its nationwide reach.
quote: ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) should be identified as being primarily responsible for enforcing civil immigration regulations

title: Rescind ICE 'sensitive zones' limits
proposal: All ICE memos naming 'sensitive zones' where agents may not operate, and other memos limiting enforcement, should be rescinded, relying on officers' judgment instead.
quote: All ICE memoranda identifying “sensitive zones” where ICE personnel are prohibited from operating should be rescinded.

title: Use expedited removal to its full legal extent
proposal: ICE should make full use of expedited removal, which it has limited to people caught within 100 miles of the border even though the law does not require that.
quote: ICE should make full use of existing Expedited Removal (ER) authorities.

title: Make ICE, HSI and CBP full Intelligence Community members
proposal: ICE/HSI and CBP should be full participants in the Intelligence Community, replacing DHS's Office of Intelligence and Analysis there.
quote: Additionally, ICE/ HSI, along with CBP , should be full participants in the Intelligence Community.

title: Use 'Blackie's warrants' for worksite raids
proposal: ICE should put 'Blackie's warrants,' civil search warrants used when agents suspect a business employs unauthorized workers, into regular use, through a joint internal memo.
quote: The use of Blackies Warrants should be operationalized within ICE.

title: Continuously vet recent arrivals, including Afghan evacuees
proposal: DHS should continuously vet and investigate many noncitizens who entered under Biden, including some Afghan evacuees.
quote: Safeguarding Americans will require not just securing the border, but

title: Fund 100,000 immigration detention beds
proposal: Congress should require and fund a large increase in ICE detention space, to 100,000 beds per day.
quote: ICE should be funded for a significant increase in detention space, raising the daily available number of beds to 100,000.

title: Fund 20,000 ICE officers and 5,000 ICE lawyers
proposal: Congress should fund at least 20,000 ICE removal officers and 5,000 ICE attorneys.
quote: Congress should fund ICE for at least 20,000 ERO officers and 5,000 Office of the Principal Legal Advisor (OPLA) attorneys.

title: Restructure USCIS fraud detection directorate
proposal: USCIS's Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate should report directly to headquarters and its directives should take priority, to make vetting and fraud detection the focus.
quote: FDNS should undergo a structural shift focused on direct reporting from the field to headquarters

title: Restore the USCIS denaturalization unit
proposal: USCIS should bring back its unit that, with DOJ, pursues cases to strip citizenship from people who obtained it by fraud.
quote: prosecuting criminal and civil denaturalization cases, in combination with the Department of Justice

title: Create a USCIS criminal enforcement unit
proposal: USCIS should create a criminal enforcement component to investigate immigration benefit fraud and prosecute cases, with attention to forced labor in temporary work visa programs.
quote: illicit means. Additionally, USCIS should create a criminal enforcement

title: Review and reverse Biden-era USCIS policies and rules
proposal: During the transition, USCIS should audit all Biden-era policies and prepare to rescind them in the first days, and draft documents to review or reverse all Biden-era regulations.
quote: Additionally, regulatory documents should be drafted to review or reverse all regulations promulgated during the Biden Administration.

title: Retrain USCIS staff at law enforcement training centers
proposal: USCIS staff should be retrained to focus on eligibility and fraud over speed, with training returned to the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers.
quote: Training should be returned to Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC), which would underscore the enforcement role of USCIS

title: Keep USCIS staff off DACA and mass parole programs
proposal: USCIS policies should keep staff from being pulled onto programs the chapter calls unlawful, such as DACA and mass parole for Afghans, Ukrainians, and Venezuelans.
quote: is not allowed to be pulled off mission work to focus on unlawful programs (DACA, mass parole for Afghans, Ukrainians, Venezuelans, etc.)

title: Bring back the public charge rule and other Trump immigration rules
proposal: USCIS should immediately propose rules restoring Trump's public charge rule and rules on temporary work visas, work permits, asylum bars, third-country transit, parole, and U visas, replacing Biden's asylum and public charge rules.
quote: The regulatory agenda should include the immediate submission of notices of proposed rulemaking for the Trump Administration’s public charge rule

title: Shorten work permit validity and end COVID flexibilities
proposal: USCIS guidance should shorten how long work permits are valid and end COVID-era flexibilities such as reusing biometrics.
quote: USCIS policy memos and operational guidance should reduce the validity of employment authorization documents and end the COVID flexibilities

title: Reject incomplete applications and require interviews
proposal: USCIS should reject incomplete applications, require fraud-unit sign-off before approvals, and return to interviewing nearly all appropriate applicants.
quote: Other efforts should be focused on adjudication standards returning to nearly 100 percent interview requirements for all appropriate cases.

title: Repeal the diversity visa lottery
proposal: As part of a merit-based immigration system, the diversity visa lottery should be repealed.
quote: luck-of-the-draw immigration. To that end, the diversity visa lottery should be repealed

title: End extended-family ('chain') immigration
proposal: Family-based immigration beyond the nuclear family ('chain migration') should be ended.
quote: chain migration should be ended while focusing on the nuclear family

title: Replace employment visas with a 'best and brightest' system
proposal: The current employment visa program should be replaced with a system that gives visas only to the most highly skilled applicants.
quote: the existing employment visa program should be replaced with a system to award visas only to the “best and brightest.”

title: Narrow who may get permission to work in the U.S.
proposal: Congress should narrow which noncitizens are eligible to work, limiting work permits to certain categories, and DHS should issue rules limiting eligible classes.
quote: action to narrow statutory eligibility to work in the United States and mitigate unfair employment competition for U.S. citizens.

title: Make H-1B an elite, highest-wage visa program
proposal: The H-1B program should be changed so employers compete to bring only top foreign workers at the highest wages, without disadvantaging U.S. workers.
quote: The oft-abused H-1B program should be transformed into an elite program through which employers are vying to bring in only the top foreign workers

title: Repeal Temporary Protected Status designations
proposal: Temporary Protected Status designations should be repealed, both by Congress and through executive action.
quote: Repeal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) designations

title: USCIS should not follow court rulings lacking jurisdiction
proposal: USCIS should state that it will not honor court decisions undermining its rules where the court lacks jurisdiction.
quote: USCIS should make it clear that where no court jurisdiction exists, it will not honor court decisions that seek to undermine regulatory and subregulatory efforts.

title: Raise USCIS fees, limit fee waivers, add asylum fee
proposal: USCIS should raise all fees, sharply limit fee waivers, and charge a fee for asylum applications; Congress should allow a 10 percent across-the-board increase.
quote: Aside from an increase in all fees, the rule should drastically limit the availability for fee waivers and should implement a fee for asylum applications.

title: Expand USCIS premium processing
proposal: USCIS should offer more paid premium processing to bring in revenue, especially if fee increases fail.
quote: USCIS should strive to increase opportunities for premium processing

title: Require denied applicants to leave immediately
proposal: Until backlogs are cleared, anyone denied an immigration benefit or status should be required to leave the U.S. immediately.
quote: all applicants rejected for any benefit or status adjudication should be required to leave the U.S. immediately.

title: Pause applications when backlogs grow too large
proposal: USCIS should stop accepting applications in a category when its backlog becomes excessive and resume once it is manageable.
quote: USCIS should pause the intake of applications in a benefit category when backlogs in that category become excessive.

title: Make USCIS a national security agency and decertify its union
proposal: USCIS and all its jobs should be classified as national security–sensitive, leaks punished, its union decertified, and employees who will not conform separated.
quote: Leaks must be investigated and punished as they would be in a national security agency, and the union should be decertified.

title: Move most USCIS staff out of Washington
proposal: USCIS should keep only a skeleton staff in D.C. and rotate operational and security staff to offices around the country.
quote: USCIS’s D.C. personnel presence should be skeletal, and agency employees with operational or security roles should be rotated out to offices throughout the United States.

title: Create a Title 42-style border expulsion power in immigration law
proposal: Congress should create an authority like the COVID-era Title 42 power to immediately expel migrants when certain non-health conditions are met, such as losing control of the border.
quote: Create an authority akin to the Title 42 Public Health authority that has been used during the COVID-19 pandemic to expel illegal aliens

title: Mandatory funding for the border wall
proposal: Congress should provide a mandatory appropriation to build more border wall systems, technology, and staffing in strategic places.
quote: Mandatory appropriation for border wall system infrastructure. The monies appropriated would be used to fund the construction of additional border wall systems

title: Repeal protections for unaccompanied migrant children (TVPRA 235)
proposal: Congress should repeal Section 235 of the TVPRA, which gives unaccompanied children immigration benefits, or amend it so children of any nationality can be quickly returned home.
quote: Congress should repeal Section 235 of the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008

title: End the Flores settlement on detaining children
proposal: Congress should end the Flores Settlement Agreement by setting national standards for detaining families and children, allowing large-scale use of temporary facilities like tents.
quote: Congress must end the Flores Settlement Agreement by explicitly setting nationwide terms and standards for family and unaccompanied detention and housing.

title: Move custody of migrant children from HHS to DHS
proposal: Congress should amend the law to move detention of migrant children from HHS to DHS.
quote: move detention of alien children expressly from the Department of Health and Human Services to DHS.

title: Raise the 'credible fear' standard for asylum seekers
proposal: The credible fear standard used at initial asylum screening should be raised to match the full asylum standard and account for credibility.
quote: The standard for a credible fear of persecution should be raised and aligned to the standard for asylum.

title: Write asylum bars and third-country transit rules into law
proposal: Congress should put the former asylum bars and the third-country transit rule into law.
quote: Codify former asylum bars and third-country transit rules.

title: Eliminate or narrow 'particular social group' asylum ground
proposal: Congress should eliminate the 'particular social group' basis for asylum or define it narrowly, at least stating that gang and domestic violence are not grounds for asylum.
quote: Congress should eliminate the particular social group protected ground as vague and overbroad or, in the alternative, provide a clear definition

title: Limit immigration parole by law
proposal: Congress should end what the chapter calls widespread parole abuse by setting specific standards and returning parole to an extraordinary remedy for very limited uses.
quote: Congress should end the widespread abuse of parole in contravention of statute and return it to its origins as an extraordinary remedy for very limited purposes.

title: Stop funding NGOs that process and transport migrants
proposal: Congress should halt funds to nonprofits that process and transport migrants and redirect the money and facilities to border security, detention, and immigration courts.
quote: Congress should halt funds given to nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) to process and transport illegal aliens into and throughout the United States.

title: Restore and strengthen 'Remain in Mexico'
proposal: Congress should update the law behind the Remain in Mexico program so it withstands court challenges, and the President should restart negotiations with Mexico to fully implement it.
quote: Update the statutory language providing the basis for the Remain in Mexico program as needed to withstand judicial scrutiny and executive inaction.

title: Require and reinstate Asylum Cooperative Agreements
proposal: Congress should require the executive branch to negotiate and keep Asylum Cooperative Agreements, and the President should immediately reinstate them with Northern Triangle countries.
quote: Congress should mandate that the executive branch work faithfully to negotiate and execute ACAs

title: Allow fast-track asylum review programs (PACR, HARP)
proposal: Congress should explicitly allow, and the President should reinstate, fast asylum review programs like PACR and HARP.
quote: Congress should explicitly permit programs akin to the Prompt Asylum Claim Review (PACR) and Humanitarian Asylum Review Process (HARP) programs.

title: Make E-Verify permanent and mandatory
proposal: Congress should permanently authorize E-Verify and require all employers to use it.
quote: Congress should also permanently authorize E-Verify and make it mandatory.

title: Authorize state and local police to enforce immigration law
proposal: Congress should clearly authorize state and local law enforcement to take part in immigration and border security actions, consistent with Arizona v. United States.
quote: Congress should unequivocally authorize state and local law enforcement to participate in immigration and border security actions

title: Require detainer compliance and penalize sanctuary jurisdictions
proposal: Congress should require compliance with ICE detainers as far as the Tenth Amendment allows and set financial penalties for sanctuary jurisdictions.
quote: Congress should require compliance with immigration detainers to the maximum extent consistent with the Tenth Amendment and set financial disincentives

title: Restrict prosecutorial discretion in immigration enforcement
proposal: Congress, and the President by executive order, should restrict prosecutorial discretion so it cannot be used as a 'catch-all' excuse to limit immigration enforcement.
quote: Congress should restrict the authority for prosecutorial discretion to eliminate it as a “catch-all” excuse for limiting immigration enforcement.

title: Make immigration detention mandatory ('shall' detain)
proposal: Congress should change immigration law language from saying noncitizens 'may' be detained to saying they 'shall' be detained.
quote: Congress should eliminate ambiguous discretionary language in Title 8 that aliens “may” be detained and clarify that aliens “shall” be detained.

title: Use all ICE detention space, including tents
proposal: An executive order should require ICE to use all detention space, report weekly on capacity, and allow temporary facilities like tents once permanent space is full.
quote: issue weekly reports on detention capacity, and provide authority for low-level temporary capacity (for example, tents) once permanent space is full.

title: End Alternatives to Detention for border crossers
proposal: Alternatives to Detention should not be used for border crossers except in rare cases approved by the Secretary.
quote: Eliminate the use of ATD for border crossers except in rare cases and only with the explicit authority of the Secretary.

title: Ban categorical parole by executive order
proposal: Parole should be allowed only when the DHS Secretary certifies a humanitarian or significant public benefit reason, and never for whole categories of people.
quote: Prohibit the use of parole except in matters that are certified by the Secretary of Homeland Security as requiring action

title: Stop government-paid travel for migrants
proposal: An executive order should ban Notices to Report, any funds for migrants' travel into the U.S. interior, and government flights or transport for them.
quote: Prohibit the use of Notices to Report, the use of any funds for travel into the interior of the United States, and government flights or transportation for aliens.

title: Require E-Verify for all federal contractors
proposal: Anyone doing business with the federal government should be required to use E-Verify.
quote: Mandate the use of E-Verify for anyone doing business with the government.

title: Give USCIS access to intelligence and police databases
proposal: USCIS should be designated 'Intelligence Community–adjacent' so it can access national security and law enforcement databases.
quote: Designate USCIS as Intelligence Community–adjacent, ensuring that it has access to national security and law enforcement databases.

title: Emergency power to block entry during a mass migration
proposal: When the Secretary finds a mass migration emergency, the Secretary, with presidential approval, could bar entry from named places and expel migrants, exempt from usual rulemaking, and waive immigration law requirements.
quote: rules and regulations prohibiting in whole or in part the introduction of persons from such countries or places as he or she shall designate

title: Open the 287(g) program to all applying jurisdictions
proposal: DHS should issue a memo saying no jurisdiction that applies to the 287(g) partnership program may be denied without good cause.
quote: Issue a memo prohibiting any jurisdiction that applies from being denied access to the program unless good cause is shown.

title: Raise FEMA's threshold for disaster aid
proposal: FEMA should raise the per capita damage threshold for public assistance, which has not kept up with inflation, or use a deductible instead.
quote: FEMA should raise the threshold because the per capita indicator has not kept pace with inflation

title: Cut the federal share of disaster costs
proposal: Congress should change disaster cost-sharing so the federal government pays 25 percent for small disasters, rising to at most 75 percent for catastrophic ones.
quote: Congress should change the cost-share arrangement so that the federal government covers 25

title: Wind down the National Flood Insurance Program
proposal: The National Flood Insurance Program should be phased out and replaced by private insurance, starting with the least risky areas.
quote: The NFIP should be wound down and replaced with private insurance starting with the least risky areas currently identified by the program.

title: Fewer Senate-confirmed FEMA posts; end 'springing Cabinet' role
proposal: Only the FEMA Administrator should need Senate confirmation, and FEMA's 'springing Cabinet position' should be eliminated.
quote: Additionally, FEMA’s “springing Cabinet position” should be eliminated, as this creates significant unnecessary challenges

title: Shed CISA's extra roles
proposal: CISA's emergency communications and chemical facility security roles should move to FEMA, its school security work should go to state offices, and it should stop duplicating other agencies' cyber work.
quote: its school security functions should be transferred to state homeland security offices; and CISA should refrain from duplicating cybersecurity functions

title: End CISA's misinformation and disinformation work
proposal: CISA should immediately end its efforts to counter misinformation and disinformation, leaving foreign actors to the Intelligence Community.
quote: Of the utmost urgency is immediately ending CISA’s counter-mis

title: Dismiss CISA's Cybersecurity Advisory Committee
proposal: All members of the CISA Cybersecurity Advisory Committee should be dismissed on the first day.
quote: In any event, the entirety of the CISA Cybersecurity Advisory Committee should be dismissed on Day One.

title: Limit CISA's election role to cyber hygiene checks
proposal: For elections, CISA should only help states and localities check the cybersecurity of their hardware and software, stay out close to elections, and not do messaging.
quote: CISA should help states and localities assess whether they have good cyber hygiene in their hardware and software in preparation for an election—but nothing more.

title: Focus the Coast Guard on U.S. home waters
proposal: The Coast Guard's mission should focus on protecting U.S. waters out to 200 miles, including against Chinese fishing fleets and drug and migrant flows, and be scaled to its long-term budget.
quote: The scope of the Coast Guard’s mission needs to be focused on protecting U.S. resources and interests in its home waters

title: Require a 30-year Coast Guard shipbuilding plan
proposal: The Coast Guard should submit to Congress a long-range shipbuilding plan like the Navy's, ideally merged into one naval plan.
quote: The Coast Guard should be required to submit to Congress a long-range shipbuilding plan modeled on the Navy’s 30-Year Shipbuilding Plan.

title: Expand Coast Guard presence in the Pacific
proposal: The Coast Guard should prioritize the Pacific, accelerate basing in American Samoa, and seek more presence in Palau, Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands.
quote: Expansion of facilities in American Samoa and basing of cutters there is one clear step in this direction and should be accelerated

title: Navy board to reset Coast Guard wartime missions
proposal: The Navy Secretary should convene a board to reset Coast Guard wartime requirements, with yearly joint Pacific drills funded by DOD.
quote: The Secretary of the Navy should convene a naval board to review and reset requirements for Coast Guard wartime mission support.

title: Create an interagency maritime coordination office
proposal: An interagency office should be set up to coordinate efforts to advance U.S. maritime interests and military and commercial competitiveness.
quote: An interagency maritime coordination office focused on developing and overseeing comprehensive efforts to advance the nation’s

title: Consider moving the Arctic mission to the Navy
proposal: The chapter suggests considering shifting the Arctic mission from the Coast Guard to the Navy, or funding it above current levels.
quote: Consideration should be given to shifting the Arctic mission to the Navy.

title: Re-vet Biden-era Coast Guard promotions; rehire vaccine refusers
proposal: The Coast Guard should drop diversity messaging, re-vet promotions and hires made under Biden, and rehire members dismissed for refusing the COVID vaccine with service time credited.
quote: USCG should also make a serious effort to re-vet any promotions and hiring that occurred on the Biden Administration’s watch

title: Close Secret Service field offices; send agents to ICE
proposal: The Secret Service should hand non-protective investigations to DOJ and Treasury, close field offices not taken over by them, and move field agents into ICE offices.
quote: It should begin the logistical operation of closing all field offices throughout the country and internationally to the extent they are not taken over by Treasury or Justice.

title: Secret Service to track money tied to illegal immigration
proposal: The only non-protective Secret Service investigations should be HSI-directed probes of financial crimes tied to illegal immigration, such as remittances and payments to smugglers.
quote: This should include tracing remittances, any funds that are used to pay coyotes or the cartels

title: Keep visitor logs wherever the President works or lives
proposal: The Secret Service should keep visitor logs for all facilities where the President works or lives.
quote: USSS should keep visitor logs for all facilities where the President works or resides.

title: Add staff to the Secret Service Uniformed Division
proposal: The Secret Service Uniformed Division needs a significant staffing increase to reduce long hours and turnover.
quote: The Uniform Division (UD) of USSS requires a significant staffing increase.

title: Let Uniformed Division officers enforce all laws in D.C.
proposal: Secret Service Uniformed Division officers should be able to enforce all applicable laws in Washington, D.C., not just near the White House.
quote: UD officers should enforce all applicable laws. The result would be to allow UD officers to gain more law enforcement experience

title: Route DHS budget messages to Congress through Legislative Affairs
proposal: All DHS budget communications to Congress, including from the CFO, should first go to the Legislative Affairs director, and appropriations liaison staff should move into that office.
quote: all budget communications from the OCFO, including from the CFO him/ herself, should first be provided to the Director of OLA

title: Have the Federal Protective Service report to the Secretary
proposal: The Federal Protective Service should report directly to the DHS Secretary and set information-sharing agreements with the Marshals, Park Police, and FBI.
quote: FPS should report to the Secretary as other components (e.g., FLETC) do.

title: Review DHS domestic terrorism programs
proposal: DHS's policy office should fully inventory and reevaluate the department's domestic terrorism efforts for consistency with the President's priorities, the law, and constitutional rights.
quote: PLCY should perform a complete inventory, analysis, and reevaluation of the department’s domestic terrorism lines of effort

title: Publish DHS work with social media on speech; remove staff involved
proposal: DHS should inventory and publicly report its work with social media companies to affect Americans' speech, and remove all personnel who took part.
quote: PLCY should likewise do a complete inventory, analysis, and evaluation of any of the department’s work, in coordination with social media outlets, to censor

title: Central policy office approval of all DHS grants
proposal: DHS's policy office should set one grant policy aligned with the President's priorities and clear every grant decision.
quote: priorities. PLCY should clear all granting decisions to ensure that they are

title: Eliminate the Quadrennial Homeland Security Review
proposal: DHS should work with Congress to streamline reporting requirements and seek to eliminate the Quadrennial Homeland Security Review.
quote: PLCY should seek the elimination of the Quadrennial Homeland Security Review.

title: Make one office the source of DHS immigration statistics
proposal: DHS should strengthen its Immigration Statistics program and make it the single source for all department immigration data.
quote: PLCY should bolster its Immigration Statistics program and make it the one-stop shop

title: Eliminate DHS's Office of Intelligence and Analysis
proposal: The DHS Office of Intelligence and Analysis should be eliminated, with a few tactical functions and staff moved to the National Operations Center.
quote: The Office of Intelligence and Analysis should be eliminated both because it has not added value

title: Have component lawyers report to component heads
proposal: Each DHS component's chief counsel should report directly to the component head and only indirectly to the DHS General Counsel.
quote: should report directly to the component head, report indirectly to the DHS General Counsel, and be accountable to the component head.

title: Hire more political appointees in DHS legal office
proposal: The DHS General Counsel's office should hire significantly more Schedule C political appointees to supervise career lawyers.
quote: OGC should hire significantly more Schedule C/political appointees who in turn supervise career staff and manage their output.

title: Buy e-discovery software for DHS lawsuits and oversight
proposal: DHS's legal office should invest in e-discovery software and a vendor, and have the IT office gather documents for congressional requests.
quote: OGC should invest in e-discovery software and contract with a vendor to manage the department’s e-discovery.

title: Merge DHS outreach office into Public Affairs
proposal: The Office of Partnership and Engagement should be merged into Public Affairs, and component communications staff should report to headquarters.
quote: The Office of Partnership and Engagement should be merged into the Office of Public Affairs.

title: Only political appointees talk to Congress for DHS
proposal: Only political appointees in DHS Legislative Affairs should deal directly with congressional staff, including on budget matters.
quote: Only political appointees in OLA should interact directly with congressional staff on all inquiries, including budget and appropriations matters.

title: Answer to only one committee per chamber
proposal: The President should seek a deal limiting DHS oversight to one authorizing and one appropriations committee per chamber; if refused, DHS should answer only to those it picks.
quote: If congressional leadership will not limit their committees’ jurisdiction over DHS, DHS should identify one authorizing and appropriations committee in each chamber and answer only to it.

title: Stop filing outdated reports to Congress
proposal: DHS should identify outdated congressional reporting requirements, tell Congress it will stop those reports, and set sunset dates for others.
quote: OLA staff should also identify outdated and needless congressional reporting requirements and notify Congress

title: Fold DHS civil rights and privacy offices into the legal office
proposal: The General Counsel's office should absorb the Civil Rights and Civil Liberties office and the Privacy Office under a political Deputy General Counsel, with civil rights complaints sent to the Inspector General.
quote: The Office of General Counsel should absorb both CRCL’s and PRIV’s necessary functions

title: Limit DHS privacy protections to citizens and green card holders
proposal: DHS documents should be updated to state that DHS protects privacy only as the Privacy Act requires, for U.S. persons and lawful permanent residents.
quote: all DHS issuances should be updated to reflect that DHS protects the privacy of individuals as required by the Privacy Act (U.S. persons and lawful permanent residents)

title: End civil rights and privacy review of DHS intelligence
proposal: DHS civil rights and privacy staff should no longer review or advise on intelligence products.
quote: CRCL and PRIV staff should no longer review intelligence products or provide guidance on any intelligence products or reports.

title: Disband civil rights and privacy advisory boards
proposal: DHS should disband outside advisory boards and over 50 working groups involving its civil rights and privacy offices, which should stop issuing bulletins.
quote: OGC should disband the outside advisory boards and the more than 50 working groups in which CRCL and PRIV currently participate.

title: Eliminate the Immigration Detention Ombudsman
proposal: The Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman should be eliminated, which requires changing the law; if it remains, CRCL should lose its immigration role.
quote: The Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman should be eliminated.

title: Eliminate the USCIS Ombudsman
proposal: The Citizenship and Immigration Services Ombudsman should be eliminated by law, with case work moved into USCIS; if it remains, it should not help unauthorized immigrants, including DACA applicants, get benefits.
quote: The Office of the Citizenship and Immigration Services Ombudsman should be eliminated.

title: Have DOD build the wall and use troops at the border
proposal: The Defense Department should help aggressively build the southern border wall and use military personnel and equipment to stop crossings between ports of entry.
quote: Assist in aggressively building the border wall system on America’s southern border.

title: Treat immigration judges as national security staff; decertify union
proposal: DOJ should move its immigration courts to DHS or treat immigration judges as national security personnel, decertify their union, and hire many more.
quote: treat the administrative law judges (immigration judges and Board of Immigration Appeals) as national security personnel, decertify their union

title: Sanction countries that refuse deportees
proposal: The State Department should impose stiff sanctions on countries that refuse to accept deportees until they actually take them back, and let DHS lead Western Hemisphere migration diplomacy.
quote: quickly and aggressively address recalcitrant countries’ failure to accept deportees by imposing stiff sanctions

title: Limit subsidized housing to citizens and green card holders
proposal: HUD should ensure only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents use or live in federally subsidized housing.
quote: Ensure that only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents utilize or occupy federally subsidized housing.

title: Deny student loans tied to in-state tuition for unauthorized immigrants
proposal: The Education Department should deny federal loans to noncitizens who are not permanent residents and to students at schools that give in-state tuition to unauthorized immigrants.
quote: deny loan access to students at schools that provide in-state tuition to illegal aliens.

title: Drop the two lowest wage levels for foreign workers
proposal: The Labor Department should eliminate the two lowest of the four prevailing wage levels for foreign workers.
quote: Eliminate the two (of four) lowest wage levels for foreign workers.

title: Share tax data on unauthorized immigrants with DHS
proposal: Treasury should issue rules to equalize taxes between citizens and work visa holders and give DHS all tax information on unauthorized immigrants.
quote: provide DHS with all tax information of illegal aliens as expeditiously as possible.
